title: [finding] The release lane's mirror has no stable referent: `changesets/action@v1` is a moving tag whose bundled `@changesets/read` is a different major from the installed one
body:
Found while implementing #5775 (aligning and pinning the `lane` job's changeset mirror). Out of that card's scope — filing rather than deciding.

## The measurement

`.github/workflows/changeset-release.yml`'s `lane` job mirrors, in bash and before install, the file scan `changesets/action` performs through `readChangesetState`. Measured 2026-08-24 on `origin/main` `0fe7d0649`, that scan exists in **two copies at different majors**, and they disagree in opposite directions:

| case | copy A: `changesets/action@v1` (v1.9.0, bundles `@changesets/read@^0.6.7`) | copy B: installed `@changesets/read@1.0.0` (via `@changesets/cli@3.0.1`) |
|---|---|---|
| `.changeset/AGENTS.md` | **counted** | ignored |
| `.changeset/CLAUDE.md` | **counted** | ignored |
| `.changeset/GEMINI.md` | **counted** | ignored |
| `.changeset/pre/*.md` | not read at all | **counted** |
| `/^README\.md$/i`, dotfiles, non-`.md` | ignored | ignored |

Copy A read from the bundle that actually executes (`dist/lt-CTruzcfj.js` at tag `v1`), verbatim:

```js
o=r.filter(e=>!e.startsWith(`.`)&&e.endsWith(`.md`)&&!/^README\.md$/i.test(e))
```

#5775 resolves this by having the mirror count the **union** of the two, which is the only rule its one consumer (the release job's clear step) admits: over-counting runs that step needlessly, under-counting skips it while the action still sees a changeset and reproduces #5442's silent lost release.

## What is still unpinned, and why that is the finding

The union is only correct while copy A's behaviour is known, and **copy A cannot be pinned from this repository**:

- `changesets/action@v1` is a **moving tag**. The maintainers can retag it at any time, and doing so silently changes the bundled reader.
- The bundle is a minified, code-split chunk. Nothing in this repo installs it, so no test can execute it and no lockfile records it.

#5775's pin therefore does the only mechanical thing available: it asserts the workflow still says `changesets/action@v1`, so a **deliberate** bump fails loudly and prompts a re-measurement. A **retag of `v1` in place changes nothing in this repository and nothing fails.** That is the gap.

## Options, not a proposal

1. Pin `uses:` to a commit SHA (`changesets/action@<sha>  # v1.9.0`). Gives the mirror a genuinely stable referent and makes every change to copy A an explicit, reviewable commit. Costs: security-patch bumps become manual, and Dependabot's `github-actions` ecosystem has to be configured to bump SHAs.
2. Leave `@v1` and accept that the union is a superset chosen to survive plausible drift in either direction, documented as such. Costs nothing; keeps a silent-retag hole that is invisible until release day.
3. Stop predicting the action's branch at all — e.g. have the clear step run unconditionally instead of behind `pending_changesets`, so no mirror is needed. Costs: rethinking why the lane job exists; benefits: deletes this whole class of drift.

Worth noting for whoever picks: `changeset-release.yml`'s own header already flags an eventual `changesets/action@v2` migration (v2's `/publish` sub-action is called out there as "plausibly the shape that makes the clear step unnecessary"), so options 1 and 3 may collapse into that work rather than being separate.

⛔ Nothing was changed by this issue. Filed unassigned.
